A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same UniVAD research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text and visual comparisons establish that differences are confined to PDF pages 1 and 9; the remaining pages are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniVAD benchmark results, module ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative wood-defect and crack-segmentation results, including in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, appendix ablations, and practical examples.

M1.justification: The C3, CAPM, and GECM procedures, anomaly-score combinations, and Appendix C adaptation using a trainable adapter are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine industrial, logical, and medical benchmarks, plus the wood-defect and CrackVision scenarios in Appendix E.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PatchCore, AnomalyGPT, WinCLIP, ComAD, UniAD, and MedCLIP. Table 2 retains DRA, BGAD, and MVFA. Comparator membership in the supplementary comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The 1-normal-shot and 4-abnormal-shot evaluations, image-level and pixel-level AUC metrics, encoders, preprocessing, and appendix shot-count and resolution settings remain identical.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D retain the same module, feature, distance, clustering, shot-count, and resolution analyses. The qualitative examples in Section 4.4 and Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate tables and plots, without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Section 5 removes v1's approximately 0.7-second inference time per image and substitutes a qualitative latency statement. Benchmark scores, ablation values, plotted trends, and qualitative detection results otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), including the appendix graph-attention formulation, are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free unified few-shot detection across industrial, logical, and medical domains, and superior performance over domain-specific methods, retain their original scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 still identifies foundation-model dependence and inference latency as limitations for real-time applications. Removing the runtime number does not change this qualitative interpretation; performance and generalization explanations are otherwise identical.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v3 states that code is available, supplies a GitHub repository link, and adds a project website. The numerical inference-time disclosure is removed. Other implementation details and appendix pseudocode are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning as the first training-free unified few-shot visual anomaly detection method remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Brief edits update the code-release statement and latency wording, add the project address, and update the arXiv version/date stamp. Section organization and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: First-page spacing and Figure 1 sizing/placement change, and the limitations paragraph reflows. No figures or tables are added or removed; their substantive content and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit code and project links make reproduction more actionable than v1's future-release promise, providing a modest improvement in reproducibility documentation. This gain is partly offset by removal of the 0.7-second/image runtime estimate, which reduces efficiency transparency. The methods, experimental evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
